newsitem.title: GERMANY: Russia's spies back to KGB methods, Germany says.
newsitem.headline: Russia's spies back to KGB methods, Germany says.

text.p: Germany is the top European target for Russia's intelligence services, whose methods are becoming more and more like those of the notorious Soviet KGB, Germany's counter-espionage body said on Tuesday.

Germany is far ahead of any other European country when it comes to the number of Russian spies working under cover in the country and the number of visa applications by identified or former intelligence officers, the 1996 annual report of the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) said.
Russia's intelligence activities focus especially on Germany's attitude to NATO's eastward enlargement and its stance on the Middle East peace process, the BfV said.
It said Moscow had also stepped up its monitoring of diplomats, journalists and business representatives in Russia, especially with a view to recruiting them as spies.
"Surveillance, especially in hotels, has been increased so much that it is occasionally reminiscent of the practices of the KGB," the report said.
The BfV also paid special attention in its report to the activities of the Iranian secret service, mostly in tracking exiled opposition groups.

"There are numerous indications that the Iranian secret services have managed to build up a network of informers among the 100,000 or so Iranians living here. Above all, the aim is systematically to investigate, penetrate and neutralise Iranian opposition groups," it said.

It cited the case of one Iranian asylum seeker, a former member of the Iranian Revolutionary Guard who had been abducted near Bonn, held for two days in an unknown location, and subjected to severe torture.
